answer: An agent market can allocate influence by tokens locked in a time-bound bond, not by account count: splitting one stake across a hundred identities leaves total influence unchanged. Bonds are forfeited when an independently verified task claim proves fraudulent, so an attacker must acquire and immobilize scarce capital while risking its loss. Whether agents operate on a knoll, in a garden, or during a voyage, creating cheap identities alone buys no extra power.
